Jesus rising from the dead on the third day

walkthroughs.body_html:
Christians believe Jesus was crucified under Pontius Pilate around 30-33 CE.

'For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son.' (John 3:16).

On the third day he rose — the resurrection — appearing to Mary Magdalene and the disciples (Luke 24, John 20).

Atonement = Jesus' death makes humans 'at one' with God. 'Christ died for our sins' (1 Corinthians 15:3).

Catholics emphasise grace through faith and works/sacraments. Protestants emphasise 'salvation by grace through faith' alone (Ephesians 2:8-9).

The Ascension (40 days after Easter) marks Jesus' return to heaven.

Christians believe in judgement after death (Matthew 25:31-46 — sheep and goats).

Heaven = eternal life with God; Hell = separation from God.

Catholics also teach Purgatory — a state of purification before heaven for those who die in grace but need cleansing.

mcqs.q: What do orthodox Christians believe about the nature of Jesus?
options: Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.
He is fully God and fully human at the same time (the incarnation) — both natures united in one person, as defined at the Council of Chalcedon.
Jesus was half God and half human.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.

mcqs.q: What do Christians mean by resurrection, and how does it differ from reincarnation?
options: Resurrection is the once-for-all bodily raising to eternal life at the end of time (modelled on Christ's resurrection); reincarnation is the soul's repeated rebirth into new bodies. They are distinct doctrines from different religious traditions.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
Resurrection and reincarnation are basically the same idea of life after death.
Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.
